text: Hello boys and girls,Astrid is here, welcome to my class again.Please get your student's book and worksheet ready.In the previous lesson, we read a text titled France is Calling.Did you go over the text and all the new words?I bet you did.I wonder how well you know about the text.Here, I have got some questions for you.Don't worry, they are quite easy.Why does the writer think Paris is beautiful?Because it has world-famous landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower and the Arc de Triomphe.And it also has wide tree-lined streets.How far is Euro Disney from the centre of Paris?Right, it's an hour away from the centre of Paris.Who does the writer suggest go to Euro Disney?What can they do there?The writer suggests parents with children go to Euro Disney.They can take different rides, enjoy the fireworks displays, take photos with cartoon characters, etc.Nowadays, how do people travel from Paris to London?How long does it take?They can travel by train through the Channel Tunnel, and it takes only three hours.Next question.What can you see and do in central France?A lot of things.We can see crops such as wheat and sunflowers.Many vineyards where grapes are grown.Probably, we could taste excellent local wines.What's more, we can also visit some scenic areas like the Loire Valley in central France.There, we can see the Loire River, the rolling countryside, and some old castles where the kings and queens of France used to live.What are the four popular French products mentioned in the text?You are right, French bread and cakes, cheese and wine.The last question.Why is France considered a leader in art and culture?Good, because a lot of young students from different countries go to France to further their studies.And every year, French film festivals, exhibitions, and concerts are organized throughout the world.France definitely leads the art and culture.So much for the revision.Hopefully, you know the answers to all the questions.Now, open your books and turn to page 93.Remember that?At the end of last lesson, we gave a subtitle to each paragraph of the text.Here's what we discussed.This time, read the text again and think about the question.How does the writer organize the text?If I'd like you to divide the text into three parts, how will you do that?And why?Well, let's listen to my student, Brauning's answer.�I think part 1 is the first paragraph, it elicits the topic, France.Part 2 should be from paragraph 2 to paragraph 5.The writer introduces different parts of France.This part is organized by geography.And the last part is paragraph 6 and 7.The writer introduces two features of France, food, culture and art.Thank you Ronin, I partly agree with you, and I'd like to share my answer with you.Part 1, paragraphs 1 to 3.Think about why I divided the text like this.Actually, paragraphs 1 to 3 are organized from general to specific.The country, the capital, then attractions for children.Paragraphs 4 and 5 are organized by geography.The country's location and regions.The last two paragraphs focus on society, food and culture.Actually, there are few organizational patterns that a text often follows.For example, paragraphs may be arranged to show time.Or sequence of events.Or spatial order.In other texts, paragraphs may be arranged in order of importance.Moving from the most important point to the least important point, or vice versa.In another common pattern, paragraphs move from the most general point to the most specific.Or from the most specific to the most general.The patterns mentioned here are most widely used in informational articles.Of course, there are many other ones.There is not a standard pattern that works for every text.However, it is important that the text follow a logical order.After talking about the patterns of organization, let's go on with our discussion on the text.Can we exchange paragraph 2 with paragraph 5?I suppose not, because the capital city is usually the most important and the best-known place in a country.Writers tend to start a text with something familiar to readers.Can the writer first tell us about the art and culture of France, then the food?I think it's okay, because there are two famous aspects or sides of France.It doesn't matter which paragraph is put ahead, as long as the ideas are clear to the readers.Do you think the text includes the must-do's or must-sees in France?Is there any important information missing?If there is, what should it be?David, can you share your opinion with us?Sure, I think the writer should have told us about the location of France like this.France is in Western Europe, since this is a text introducing traveling in France.And the writer first introduces Paris, the capital.Actually, Paris is in the northern part of France.Then the writer talks about the center of France.According to geography, after central France comes southern France.Maybe that's the information the writer has missed.Good point.The southern part of France is missing.Kalista, I know you are quite familiar with the south of France, since you have been there.Can you introduce the south of France to us?Yes, of course.The south of France lies on the coast, and it is famous for its wonderful beaches.A French town by the sea is the perfect place for a summer holiday.But if you prefer to visit France in winter, you can try skiing on the mountains in the French Alps.Thank you.So the French Alps are located in the south as well?Sounds exciting.It seems that the south of France is worth visiting too.Now, the text seems complete, from the north to the center, and then to the south.The spatial order is clearly followed.Okay, let's turn back to the text France is calling.Look at these sentences.Have you noticed the POV that is point of view in the text?The writer uses the second person point of view, right?Why does he do so?Using you as the subject gives the feeling that the writer is talking to his readers.The distance between the writer and the readers is shortened.用第二人稱敘述手法能拉近作者與讀者間的距離。The readers can feel more connected and involved in what the writer is talking about.So when you read the text, do you feel the urge to spread your wings and visit France?I bet you do.That is what the writer wants to achieve.So what do you think is the writer's purpose?To encourage people to visit France.To inform people of France's culture and history.One more question.Can you get enough information from the text if you want to visit France?You don't need to tell me the answer right now.I have a task for you to complete.Can you find the following information in the text?Read the information and tick yes or no.That is task one on your worksheet.Ready?Look at the answers.After reading the text, can you find where the Channel Tunnel information?Let me show you an example.Look at the picture.Lonely Planet.Have you ever heard of it?I guess few.You are not old enough to travel alone.What can be found in this book?Look at the words at the bottom of the left side.Pull out map.Top sides.Local secrets.Jennifer, what do you think we can find in the book?Probably we can get a map of France, some detailed information about interesting places in France.We can also get to know something that few people know about France.Great!What's inside?Are you curious?Let's open the book and take a close look at the contents.How many pages are there in the book?More than one thousand pages.Just about a single country.Obviously, it contains a really large amount of information.And the information is in full detail.Inside the book, you will find color maps and images throughout the book.You can find the maps of even the smallest towns, highlights and itineraries.The writer will recommend the best, most interesting or most exciting part of France to you.And he will also help you create your ideal trip.Here are two itineraries.A week trip around Paris and a five-day trip along the Loire Valley.In the book, the writer offers some insider tips too.Insider tips are tips from expert authors with which you are able to save time and money and get around like a local, avoiding crowds and dangerous places.As for essential information, here's some about the Eiffel Tower.It tells us the opening times of the tower and the prices of different tickets.Now, you know where you can find detailed information about your travel destination.Right, it's a travel guide.So is our text a travel guide?I don't think so.I think it's a travel article.The travel guide gives practical information so you can plan your visits.But there's still something in common between a travel article and a travel guide.What is it?Yes, they both give us some useful information which enables us to make a travel plan.Okay, it's time for practice.You are going to make a three-day travel plan in France for a family of four, including two children.The family are not on a package tour, of course.Since your time is quite limited, you only need to make a rough and simple plan.Tell me, what do you usually include in your travel plan, David?I usually make a list first.I write down the places I want to visit, including restaurants, museums, malls and other places of interest, and mark them on a map.I also list things I want to do and how I'm going to get around.Wow, you are a travel expert.Good idea.We need to write down where to go, what to see or do, and for foodies, what to eat.I believe the text France is calling will help you in a way, because it contains lots of information on travel in France.Though it's a little bit general.Remember, it's only a three-day trip in France.Plan your trip well.And to save time, please make your plan in a note form.A table, a mind map, a tree map or an outline.It's up to you.But remember, you must tell itinerary seems a little bit hurried, because within just three days, the family have to go from north to south.Then, let's look at the second one by Ronnie.It's like an outline, isn't it?I'm so happy
